chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿUthmān al-Nawwāʾ, from one whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, afflicts the believer with every affliction, and causes him to die by every kind of death, but He does not afflict him with the loss of his intellect.
Do you not see Ayyūb, how Iblīs was given power over his wealth, over his children, over his family, and over everything belonging to him, yet he was not given power over his intellect.
It was left for him so that he might affirm the tawhid of Allah by means of it.

key_terms.أَيُّوبَ: Prophet Ayyūb عليه السلام, cited as an example of patient trial
key_terms.إِبْلِيسُ: Iblīs, who was given limited power over external matters
key_terms.اللَّهَ: Allah, the One whose tawhid is recognized through intellect
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer who is subjected to divine trials
key_terms.ذَهَابِ عَقْلِهِ: the loss of his intellect or reasoning faculty
key_terms.عَقْلِهِ: his intellect, preserved as the basis of faith and recognition
key_terms.لِيُوَحِّدَ: so that he may affirm divine unity

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah test a believer with hardships but preserve his intellect?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a believer may be tried with severe worldly afflictions, yet the preservation of intellect is a special divine favor. By the example of Ayyūb عليه السلام, it shows that intellect remains the means by which one maintains tawhid and recognition of Allah even amid extreme suffering.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Usman Al Nawwa’a, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Afflicts the Momin with every affliction, and Causes him to died with every (kind of) death, but Heazwj does not Afflict him with the departure of his intellect.

But, do you not see Ayoub<sup>as</sup> how Iblees<sup>la</sup> overcame upon his<sup>as</sup> wealth, and upon his<sup>as</sup> children, and upon his<sup>as</sup> wife, and upon everything from him<sup>saww</sup> but could not overcome upon his<sup>as</sup> intellect.
It was left for him<sup>as</sup> in order for him to (understand) the Oneness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with it’.
en.sarwar: 22. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Uthman al-Nawa’ from those he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, sets the believers into trials of all kinds and causes them to die by all kinds of deaths but He does not make them suffer the loss of their power of reason.
Consider (prophet) Ayyub (Job) how Iblis (the devil) controlled his property, children, wife and all things that were his but had no control over his power of reason,
which was left for him to maintain his belief in Allah only.”
